title: A Sigil for the Veil
premise: Cyrus Brightwater makes his living cutting memories from the minds of the desperate and selling them to collectors — until the night he steals a memory that belongs to a dead god. The old gods of Thornfell, long silent, are waking, and the stolen memory is the sigil that can seal or unmake the veil between their realm and the living world. Hunted by the god's zealots and betrayed by the found family of smugglers he trusted with everything, Cyrus discovers he is not a man at all but a fabricated memory given flesh, created to carry the sigil across a border drawn through a country that no longer exists. In the end, he must choose between erasing himself to restore the veil or tearing it open to keep the only family he has ever known.
about_author: Beatrix Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. She writes fantasy about people made of other people's stories, and lives somewhere with too much rain.

chapters.title: The Memory Broker's Debt
chapters.summary: Cyrus Brightwater's POV. On a smuggler's run through the Thornfell passes, Cyrus lifts a sealed memory from a dying pilgrim and finds inside it a living god's name — and a voice that answers back. His crew of smugglers, the only family he trusts, begins asking dangerous questions. The emotional beat: unease blooming into wonder as Cyrus realizes the old gods are listening again, and that something about the memory feels terrifyingly familiar.

chapters.title: What the Zealots Carry
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with an interlude from Sera, the crew's captain. The god's zealots descend on Thornfell, burning villages to recover the sigil, and Sera sells Cyrus out to save the crew — or so it appears. Fleeing alone, Cyrus learns the stolen memory contains his own face, standing at a door in a country erased from every map. The emotional beat: betrayal and vertigo as his identity begins to unravel.

chapters.title: A Door in the Vanished Country
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Sera's POV alternating, as Sera returns, confessing the betrayal was staged to fool the zealots. Together they cross into the ghost-country, where the dead nation's memories still stand like buildings, and Cyrus faces the truth: he was made from stolen memories, a vessel built to carry the sigil to the door. The emotional beat: grief transfigured into fierce love — he was fabricated, but the family that chose him is real.

chapters.title: The Sigil and the Veil
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV at the climax. At the door of the vanished country, the god offers Cyrus a bargain: erase himself, restore the veil, and his crew lives free — or tear the veil open and keep everything, at the world's cost. Cyrus chooses a third path, splitting the sigil between himself and the crew who claim him as their own. The veil holds, imperfectly, and Cyrus walks out of the mountains as something new: a man who chose his own memories. The emotional beat: sacrifice answered by found family.
